kok_maddesi: Back to library EtymArab ḪLQ خلق BP – • HDAL • © SG | created 15Feb2021, last updated 22Dec2025 √ḪLQ “root” ▪ ḪLQ_1 ‘to create, shape, form, mold’ ↗ ḫalaqa ; ‘creatures; people, man, mankind; physical constitution’ ↗ ḫalq ; ‘innate peculiarity, natural disposition, character, temper, nature’ ↗ ḫul(u)q ; ‘to invent, contrive, fabricate, concoct; to attribute falsely’ ↗ ĭḫtalaqa ▪ ḪLQ_2 ‘portion, share’ ↗ ḫalāq ▪ ḪLQ_3 ‘morals, ethics’ ↗ ʔaḫlāq ▪ ḪLQ_4 ‘shabby, threadbare, worn (garment)’ ↗ ḫalaq ▪ ḪLQ_5 ‘to aromatize, perfume ( -h s.th.)’ ↗ ḫallaqa ▪ ḪLQ_6 ‘to become angry’ ↗³ taḫallaqa ▪ ḪLQ_7 ‘caldron, boiler, kettle’ ↗ ḫalqīn ♦ Semantic value spectrum in ClassAr (acc. to BAH2008): ‘to create, originate, design, creation, the entire creation, the human race; natural disposition, innate nature; to be shapely, comely; to deal tactfully with others, assume a certain disposition; to attribute falsely; to estimate; to be of good character; luck, share; to be capable; (of a garment) to wear out; a fragrant substance’ ▪ With the exception of the loanword [v7] ḫalqīn ‘caldron, boiler, kettle’ (and prob. also [v5]), all other values may ultimately be related to each other, despite the stunning semantic variety within the root, all going back to a primary sense of *‘(to make) even, smooth’, as proposed by Palache1959: 32. The author suggested to connect the 2-3 main values along a hypothetical line of semantic development such as *‘[v4] smooth > smooth stone > small stones used to distribute lots > [v2] lot, portion, share… [which we may extend to] … > to measure > [v1] to shape, mold > to compose, create > creation, nature, constitution > character, temper > [v3] morals, ethics’ – a bit contrived, perhaps, but not unconceivable! For [v5] and [v6] see below. – Alternatively, one will have to assume at least two etyma, of different origins: one *[v2] ‘to divide, measure’ (> [v1] ‘to shape, mold, create’ > [v3] ‘morals’), and another one *‘to disappear (Akk), perish (Akk, Ug, Hbr, Gz), flee (Akk) > ‘to be absent (Ug), [v4] be consumed, worn out, threadbare (Akk, Ar), to finish, be finished (Tña, Amh, Gur, Arg), to die without having been slaughtered (Te)’ > ‘bad’ (Akk, Ug), ‘underwear’ (nHbr, JP), ‘clothing, garment’ (Mhr, Ḥrs, Soq)’. In this case, the place of Ar ‘smooth, polish, shine’ (cf. Hbr ḥālaq ‘to be united, smooth’) would not be totally clear: from *‘shaping, molding’ or from *‘wearing out’? The authors of DRS see [v2] Ar ḫalāq ‘share, lot (of happiness)’ together with [v1] ḫalaqa ‘to form, compose, create’ and ‘to make smooth, even’ (as DRS #ḪLQ-2), and distinguish these from #ḪLQ-1 / [v4] Ar ‘to be worn out’. ▪ [v1] : The basic notion underlying the variety of sub-values assembled sub [v1] is *‘shaping, molding, creating’. This value gave not only ‘creation, creature > nature, character, temper’ etc., but also more specific interpretations of the latter, like ‘good-natured, kind’ on the one side, and values like ‘fabricated, invented, concocted’ or [v6] ‘(ill-temper =) rage’ on the other; a neutral development from ‘nature, character, temper’ is [v3] ‘morals, ethics’. – As mentioned in the initial paragraph, [v1] may ultimately have emerged from [v4] via [v2]. ▪ [v2] : On account of the Hbr, Syr, Ar, and Gz evidence, Kogan2015 (118 #11) reconstructs a hypothetical C/EthSem * ḫlḳ ‘to divide, measure’. DRS sees this value immediately\unquestionably together with [v1] and [v4] when the authors list [v2] ḫalāq »part de bonheur attribué« together with both [v1] ḫalaqa »mesurer, former, composer, créer« and [v4] »rendre lisse, uni«. Cf., however, Jeffery1938 who regarded ḫalāq as a borrowing for CanSem. – For the possible dependence (according to Palache1959) of [v2] on [v4], see introductory paragraph of this CONC section. ▪ [v3] : It is right that the pl. ʔaḫlāq ‘morals, ethics’ has somehow gained a “life of its own”. Etymologically, however, it is clearly derived from [v1] ‘to create > creature > nature, temper’. ▪ [v4] : According to Palache1959, this value possibly represents the primary value in the root as a whole, though not in the modern negative sense of ḫalaq ‘shabby, threadbare, worn (garment)’ but in that of ClassAr items like † ḫaliqa ( a , ḫalaq ) ~ ḫaluqa ( u , ḫulūq , ḫulūqaẗ , ḫalāqaẗ ) ‘to be even, smooth (wood)’, † ḫulāq ‘polish, shining’, etc. (see below, section HIST). – For ideas about the hypothetical devolopment *[v4] > [v2] > [v1] > [v3], see above, introductory paragraph. ▪ [v5] : The value ‘to aromatize, perfume ( -h s.th.)’ of the D-stem ḫallaqa seems to be denominative-applicative from † ḫilāq ~ † ḫalūq ‘yellow perfume, compound of saffron’, prob. a borrowing from Lat colchicon ‘autumn crocus, C. autumnale’ kolχikón ‘colchicum’ Colchis , Grk Kólχis , the ancient region on the eastern edge of the Black Sea, famous for the Argonauts saga, the Golden Fleece and the sorceress Medea, identical with the Georgian province of Mingrelia; at least C. laetum is native to the Caucasus region – Genaust1976, s.v. »Cólchicum«. However, it is hard to imagina that Ar ḫalūq ~ ḫilāq actually designated the ‘colchicum, autumn crocus’, as the latter is poisonous. Dozy1927 mentions † ḫalūq as ‘aromate’, adding that « [l]e mot valencien haloch , qui semble dérivé de ce mot arabe, désigne le bupleurum ». But this equation does not help much either – the ‘bupleurum’ is a genus with about 190 species, none of which seems to have functioned as aromatic. – Semantic contamination with [v4] *‘smoothening, softening’ is not unCONCeivable. The obsol. PP II † muḫallaq mostly meant ‘aromatised’ wine . ▪ [v6] : The meaning ‘to become angry’ of the Ar tD-stem ³ taḫallaqa (as well as the older Gt-stem † ĭḫtalaqa VIII) is ultimately based on [v1], cf.
